x: The early leader was Mike Parker (Brighton & Hove) with Carl, closely followed by Brian Armstrong (Ilford), leading the rest. It was good to see Derek Howie on one of his trips from Stirling.
Held on the usual undulating course it was Mike Parker of New Zealand who led from the start and was over a minute clear of Lawton at half way.
Carl had a slight lead from Mike Parker(a New Zealander competing for Brighton) at 15 miles. Of the seven teams Surrey W.C. appeared to have the edge, but our team was pressing hard.
To the race itself, the early leaders were Olly Flynn, Mike Parker, Brian Adams and Amos Seddon with Carl not too far back. The team race looked good for Ilford A.C. who had many well up.
Mike Parker of Brighton was second in 12:22.8; Carl Lawton retained his third place of last year in a time of 12:37.7; only a second outside his personal best.
This was to be the race that Don Thompson's 19 year old record for the course was going to be broken by the new 50kms champion, Mike Parker.

New Zealander Mike Parker (Brighton) and D. Jarman (S.W.C.) were soon clear of the field and as the race progressed the further ahead they were and at the finish we had to wait nearly 2½ minutes before the third man arrived.

1.M.Parker (Br.) 90.08; 2.D.Jackson (York P) 92.28; 3.A.Seddon (Enf) 92.36; 7.R.Dorman 94.48; 10.C.Lawton 95.11; 24.J.Hall 98.18; 37.J.Newnham 101.21; 54.E.Crossingham 105.02; 71.J.Bromley 109.38; 74.D.Fotheringham 110.25; Results: 1.Leic W.C. 30 pts; 2.York Postal 48; 3.Sheffield 51; 4th Bels 68.
A fine win for Phil Vesty (Leic) in the second fastest time ever, followed home by Mike Parker (Brighton). Carl was first home in 6th place and Richard three places down.
Mike Parker showing the form of a few years ago won confortably leaving Paul Warburton to make an impression and get his first open placing.
